section_summary.extract_value: This section reports that ethnic identity (MEIM) is positively associated with body appreciation (BAS) and has small-to-moderate associations with self-esteem and appearance evaluation; MEIM also shows small negative associations with eating-, shape-, and weight-related concerns. The authors tested mediation by Western beauty ideal internalization (SATAQ-3 Internalization-General) and found it mediated relations between ethnic identity and eating, shape, and weight concerns (95% CIs reported), but not the relation between ethnic identity and body appreciation.
section_summary.evidence_source: As hypothesized, ethnic identity, as measured by the MEIM, was positively  associated with body appreciation (BAS); women with higher ethnic identification also reported greater body appreciation. Based on 95% confidence intervals for the indirect effects, Western beauty ideal internalization mediated the relation between ethnic identity and eating concern (−.35, −.01), ethnic identity and shape concern (−.56, −.01), and ethnic identity and weight concern (−.60, −.02). No mediating relation was found for ethnic identity and body appreciation (−.01, .24).
